name: Emerson Electric Co.

profile.description: Emerson Electric is a global automation technology company supplying measurement instruments, valves, control systems (DeltaV, Ovation), test & measurement (NI) and industrial software (AspenTech) to process, hybrid and discrete industries [1][3]. Having exited Climate Technologies (FY2023 discontinued-operations income of $10.9B) and absorbed AspenTech and NI, it is now a focused automation pure-play under CEO Lal Karsanbhai [7]. In Q3 FY2026 underlying orders rose 7%, backlog excluding AspenTech rose 7% to $8.2B, and management raised FY2026 guidance to ~5% sales growth, ~$6.55 adjusted EPS and ~$3.6B free cash flow [1]. Q4 FY2026 results and initial FY2027 guidance are due November 4, 2026 [8]. Market cap ~$92B.

innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Emerson has reshaped itself from a diversified conglomerate into an automation and industrial-software company — selling Climate Technologies (booking $10.9B of discontinued-operations income in FY2023) and building a ~$1.6B software business around AspenTech and NI [3][7]. AI Deployment (2/2): Three AI-enabled products are shipping — Nigel (test & measurement, moving from AI assistant to 'AI author'), Ovation Virtual Advisor and Aspen Virtual Advisor — which Karsanbhai calls steps toward agentic AI [3]. Market Share (1/2): A leading process-automation vendor, but it competes with Siemens, ABB, Honeywell and Rockwell and no share-gain data was found. Product Pipeline (1/2): An ~$11.2B project funnel and the stated agentic-AI roadmap give visibility, but no dated next-generation launches with revenue targets were disclosed [6][3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D is not broken out in the income statement data reviewed, so no peer comparison could be evidenced [7].
innovation.label: DEVELOPING

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Emerson's purpose — 'drive innovation that makes the world healthier, safer, smarter and more sustainable' — is clear and connected to essential industries, though not highly distinctive among automation peers [4][5]. Community Impact (2/2): The 2025 Sustainability Report (May 2026) details a $200 million, 10-year pledge to education in its operating communities, alongside a 49% cut in Scope 1+2 emissions since 2021 and a second consecutive CDP 'A' climate rating [4]. Employee Retention (1/2): The company reports a 78.9% employee-engagement score and a 0.25 TRIR, and has run a global culture survey to shape its employee value proposition — solid but not evidence of exceptional tenure [4][5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was found for the last 12 months.
inspiration.label: DEVELOPING

infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth-sleeve stock (dividend yield ~1.35% is below the 2% Dividend threshold): 8.13/10, rounded to 8. D/E of 67.7% scores 1.0; ROE of 12.8% scores 0.85 at 2x weight; revenue growth of 7.0% scores 0.90; revenue CAGR of 8.6% scores 0.91 at 2x weight — derived from FMP as the FY2021–FY2025 4-year CAGR on restated continuing operations, because FY2020 still included the divested Climate business; forward P/E of 22.72 scores 0.93; profit margin of 13.8% scores 0.69; Yahoo's PEG of 1.91 scores 0.54 at 2x weight (FMP's forward PEG is higher at ~3.3, which would score 0) [7]. Liquidity is ample at ~$439M of average daily dollar volume.
infrastructure.label: STRONG

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): PROTECTED. The hardware core — sensors, valves, actuators and DeltaV/Ovation control systems running plants — is physical and safety-critical, and AI-driven data-center and power build-outs add demand [1]. However, analysts flag the 'AI disruption narrative' as a valuation risk for the ~$1.6B software business; Karsanbhai defended it at the February 2026 Barclays conference by citing three moats that distinguish its domain-specific engineering software from generic AI that "produces answers based on inference" [3]. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI-enabled products (Nigel, Ovation Virtual Advisor, Aspen Virtual Advisor) are commercial, and Software & Systems led Q3 FY2026 order growth [1][3].
ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK

infinite_game.summary: Emerson shows strong infinite-game traits: leadership was willing to sell a large, profitable legacy business and stake the company's future on automation software and AI, and it frames competition with generic AI around improving domain depth. The purpose is well articulated and backed by measurable sustainability and community commitments. Its Just Cause is still more corporate strategy than a cause people sacrifice for, and the cultural integration of software acquisitions remains a work in progress [3][4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The purpose of making essential industries 'healthier, safer, smarter and more sustainable' connects products to tangible societal outcomes and is referenced in strategy and sustainability reporting, but it has not yet been tested as a cause that endures beyond the current portfolio [4][5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): A 78.9% engagement score, low injury rate and culture-survey-driven employee programs indicate a stable organization, but there is no evidence of exceptional psychological safety, and integrating AspenTech and NI cultures is ongoing [4][5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Rather than dismissing AI-native competitors, Karsanbhai has engaged the challenge directly, articulating where Emerson's domain software must stay better than generic AI and shipping AI products in response — competition framed as a spur to improve [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Exiting Climate Technologies — a large, profitable legacy franchise — to concentrate on automation and software is a genuine reinvention of a 130-plus-year-old company, executed in service of a clearer automation mission [3][7].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Leadership accepted near-term disruption — portfolio divestitures, large software acquisitions and integration costs — to build long-term capability, and continues investing in AI products despite investor skepticism about software multiples [3][7].

investment_thesis: Emerson is now a focused automation and industrial-software leader with improving momentum: Q3 FY2026 underlying orders grew 7% led by Software & Systems, backlog ex-AspenTech rose 7% to $8.2B, and management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance to ~$6.55 with ~$3.6B of free cash flow [1]. Trailing earnings growth of 23%, a 20%+ EBIT margin, D/E of ~68% and three commercial AI products give it both financial durability and exposure to power, LNG and AI data-center build-outs [3][7].
thesis_continued: Valuation is the main constraint: at ~36x trailing and ~22.7x forward earnings with a PEG near 1.9, the ~$165 share price prices in continued margin expansion [7]. Revenue growth is only ~5–7%, ROE of 12.8% trails the 15% target, the Middle East conflict is a ~$25M quarterly revenue headwind, and any loss of confidence in the software moats versus generic AI could compress the multiple [1][3]. The November 4 Q4 report and first FY2027 guide are a near-term test [8].
key_catalysts: Q4 FY2026 results and initial FY2027 guidance on November 4, 2026 — last year's initial guide was raised twice [8]
Conversion of the $8.2B backlog (ex-AspenTech) and ~$11.2B project funnel tied to power, LNG and AI data-center automation [1][6]
Progression of Nigel and the Virtual Advisor products toward agentic AI, supporting software growth and mix-driven margin expansion [3]
key_risks: Premium valuation (~36x trailing, ~22.7x forward, PEG ~1.9) leaves little room for a soft FY2027 guide [7]
AI-disruption narrative around the ~$1.6B software business could pressure the multiple even if fundamentals hold [3]
Macro and geopolitical exposure: ~$25M per-quarter Middle East revenue headwind, plus China and European industrial weakness [1][3]

backlog.note: Backlog excluding AspenTech was $8.2B at the end of Q3 FY2026 (June 2026), up 7% YoY [1]. Emerson does not disclose a TTM book-to-bill; underlying orders (+7%) outpacing guided sales growth (~5%) implies book-to-bill modestly above 1.0, hence yellow. ~1.75 quarters of revenue coverage reflects a largely short-cycle instruments/valves mix.
